seo.meta_title: 휘파람 Meaning | Why Koreans Say Don't Whistle at Night
seo.meta_description: AI says 휘파람 means 'whistle' and stops. It misses the superstition: whistling at night calls snakes. Learn 휘파람 불다 and the old saying.

ai_failure.situation: You're whistling in the evening at a Korean friend's home, and their grandmother tells you to stop. You ask AI why.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Explains that 휘파람 means 'whistling' and that whistling may simply be noisy.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: Many older Koreans grew up with the saying that whistling at night brings snakes (some say ghosts). The grandmother isn't calling you rude; she's repeating a superstition. BLACKPINK's 2016 song 휘파람 (English title 'Whistle') uses the word.

natural_solution.rule: 휘파람 is always 휘파람을 불다 (to blow a whistle with your mouth). If an elder stops you at night, it's the superstition — just stop, no need to apologize at length.

alternatives.context: 'You're good at whistling!' — polite compliment; 불다 becomes 부시다
The superstition: 'Whistle at night and snakes come out'
A whistle as an object — a referee's or PE teacher's whistle. Not 휘파람

nuance: Korean separates the mouth whistle (휘파람) from the object (호루라기). Night-time superstitions like this one, along with not cutting nails at night, are things younger Koreans may laugh at but still know.
